left.tested_scope: Executable crash-consistency state machine with durable attempt/cell intents, stable content-bound cell IDs, reconcile-before-execute, immutable local outcomes and deterministic certification. The controller was actually SIGKILLed at six exact boundaries. Across all six recoveries a deterministic SQLite-backed three-cell provider simulator produced exactly three execute effects; remote-effect/local-outcome crashes reconciled rather than re-executed; certificate digest was stable; and a second fresh-process certify caused zero additional provider execute/reconcile calls. Scope is limited to a local provider model with authoritative stable idempotency keys and does not establish equivalent behavior for arbitrary real providers without durable idempotency or reconciliation.

right.tested_scope: Optimistic active source-identification audit in a correctly specified Gaussian v-dominant bandit: four arms, s=25, two v=1 and two v=100, T=200, gamma=0.95, P0=25, selected-arm observation only. Per-arm discrete Gaussian-mixture inference over v in {1,100} used hypothesis-specific Kalman states and a >=0.995 posterior semantic-confidence gate after >=4 observations; otherwise a shared/base CAUSE tracker used v=10,s=25. A calibrated one-step diagnostic-information policy was evaluated on 300 held-out seeds. Active hard gating improved discounted regret versus always-shared (168.754 vs 187.318; paired-bootstrap mean difference -18.564, 95% CI [-28.980,-8.805]) but was materially worse than family BMA (active minus BMA +33.703, 95% CI [22.101,46.489]). Confident semantic errors were 3/53170 with Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound 0.0001649. This is an optimistic scientific decision-value test; it does not inherit the prior family-misspecification safety certificate and is not evidence of crash consistency, idempotent effect recovery, Chat-native dependency elimination, zero-quota replay, or protected-primary execution replacement.
